samples.text: So here we go. I think we should all be steadfast defenders of multilateralism. As Strobe Talbott reportedly remarked, "Multilateralism is hell and can be a real pain in the neck, but it is the best option for humanity as a whole." We need multilateralism in order to address our shared agenda, ranging from conflicts and climate change to sustainable development and artificial intelligence. Currently, however, we seem to be going the other way. more towards a non-cooperative and multipolar world order. This order, as it turns out, is based on zero-sum deals, transactions, and unrestrained power. This is a short-sighted approach. Tempting as it may be for some, such a multipolar order will ultimately lead to conflict. It will turn against us, whether you represent a great power, a middle power, or a small state like Finland. Between these two approaches, there's, of course, a third option, plurilateralism. It means building ad hoc coalitions when global cooperation is unattainable. And this is my first observation today, the emergence of flexible forms of cooperation around different themes and interests, be it in the economy, climate, defense, or technology. Coalition building can be a force of good, but with one condition. It should not challenge multilateralism, but build on it. It should support the UN system, not substitute it. The Coalition of the Willing for Ukraine is particularly close to my heart. It's a group of countries working to end Russia's war of aggression. The war is unlawful, unjustified, and unprovoked. Its solution will have far-reaching consequences for Ukraine and beyond. It is really about upholding international rules. The coalition works for a just and lasting peace in Ukraine in accordance with the UN Charter. It seeks to uphold the basic tenets of the international order. My second observation is that everywhere I travel around the world, I hear the word realignment. Realignment. Whether it is in Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Asia, or the Americans, nations are seeking new alliances and partnerships. This is a logical consequence in times of uncertainty and transformation.
